As soon as the website becomes big enough that investors start to take a keen interest in it Voat will most likely follow in Reddit's and Diggs footsteps.

Reddit has changed its policies to make it more attractive to advertisers by removing hate and harassing subs. Everybody left Digg because they changed their policy to a "follow" model like Twitter, with favoritism shown to sites that Digg could get revenue from. People want a forum where they can share anything they want without outside influence and so when these big changes happen people find something new.

If Voat gets big enough, I suspect they will do the same - but by then another site will be up and we will all migrate over there!
